corrected_value.title: ‘Mindreading’ Mammals? Attribution of Belief Tasks With Dolphins

decisions.quote:
When we designed our FBT study, our goal was to replicate the study conducted by Tschudin (2001,
2006) using the same methodology. For this reason, we did not seek to modify or improve the methodology.
decisions.reason: Addressing the competing_supported_matches flag between Tschudin (2001) and Tschudin (2006): although the authors also incorporate controls from Tschudin's (2006) follow-up report on the same dolphins, they explicitly state throughout the abstract, case study methods, and conclusion that their experiment was designed to replicate Tschudin (2001, 2006), directly adopt procedural specifications from Tschudin (2001) (e.g., scheduling 12 displacement trials and planning 4 FBT trials), and test Tschudin's (2001) positive claim that four dolphins passed the nonverbal false belief task. Both the shipped row and blind target 0 rightly identify Tschudin (2001) as a tested original.

decisions.quote:
After a total of nine months with over 1000 training and probe trials, the dolphin never achieved the
standard criterion set for acceptable performance (Table 3, Figure 1). Despite all of these trials, trying to train
a concept- naïve dolphin resulted in a failure to demonstrate competency at invisible displacement of a fish in
containers and to provide experimental evidence of ToM using the FBT.
decisions.location: A Case Study - Attempted Replication, lines 634-637
decisions.reason: Whereas Tschudin (2001) reported that four dolphins passed the nonverbal FBT, the present replication explicitly frames its result in the title and text as a failure to replicate: the tested dolphin failed to achieve criterion on preliminary invisible displacement trials, scored 0/2 on the FBT trials, and failed to provide experimental evidence of ToM. Methodological critiques explaining why dolphins fail the task do not alter the explicit failed verdict.

decisions.quote:
In our attempt to replicate Tschudin (2001, 2006), two adult male bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops
truncatus) and their trainers (5 and 20 years of experience, respectively) were selected.
decisions.location: A Case Study - Attempted Replication, lines 570-571
decisions.reason: The authors collected new experimental data with bottlenose dolphins at SeaWorld San Antonio to re-test the nonverbal false belief task findings of Tschudin (2001, 2006), making this a replication.
